Define quarterly business objectives, KPIs, and budget envelopes
body: Acting as the owner/board for the LeadGen AI business, define the top-line objectives for the next quarter: revenue target, number of paid customers, qualified-pipeline volume, and activation/retention goals. For each objective specify the measuring KPI (e.g., PAID_CUSTOMERS, MRR, lead-to-meeting conversion rate), a numeric target, and the accountable profile. Set hard budget envelopes for model/API spend, voice-call spend, and infrastructure spend, and state the deployment authorization rule (who may approve production releases) and kill-switch conditions. Acceptance criteria: a concise objectives document where every objective has a measurable target and budget cap, deployment authorization is explicitly assigned, and the whole document fits on two pages.

title: Audit product codebase and produce end-to-end gap analysis
body: Inventory the current state of the LeadGen AI product: backend services, admin dashboard, customer dashboard, agent tools, integrations, database schema and migrations, and known bugs. Map each component against the core SDR flow (lead ingestion -> enrichment -> qualification -> outreach -> meeting booking -> payment) and record what exists, what works, and what is broken or missing. Produce a gap analysis identifying the smallest set of fixes and features needed to make that flow work end-to-end. Acceptance criteria: a component inventory table, a list of blocking defects with reproduction steps, and a prioritized gap list tagged P0/P1/P2.

title: Audit infrastructure reliability, backups, and observability
body: Assess whether the platform can run 24/7: verify Docker/VPS setup, CI/CD pipelines, worker and queue configuration (Redis), database backup and restore procedures, health checks, logging/metrics/traces coverage, alerting, and the rollback runbook. Identify single points of failure and missing observability. Output a findings report where each finding has a severity rating and a concrete remediation step, ordered by risk. Acceptance criteria: the report covers deploy pipeline, backup/restore (with a tested restore path or a note that it is untested), monitoring, alerting, and rollback; no finding lacks a severity and a fix.

title: Run security, compliance, and QA baseline audit
body: Establish the safety baseline before any production release: review RBAC and tenant isolation, idempotency and duplicate-send protection in outbound messaging, rate limits, DND/suppression handling, voice-call policy compliance, and payment-flow safety. Inventory existing unit/integration/E2E test coverage, run the available suites, and record results. Output a compliance and QA report giving a verdict of PASS, PASS_WITH_RISK, FAIL, or BLOCKED per control area, listing any failing tests with failure details, and flagging veto-worthy items that must be fixed before release. Acceptance criteria: every control area has a verdict, all failures are enumerated, and release-blocking items are explicitly marked.

title: Synthesize audits into prioritized execution roadmap with owners
body: Using the board objectives document and the three audit reports (product gap analysis, infrastructure findings, security/QA verdicts), synthesize a single prioritized execution roadmap. Order work by dependency and risk: security/QA blockers first, then P0 product gaps, then platform reliability items, then growth work. Assign each roadmap item to exactly one owning profile (engineering, platform, guardian, hunter, sales, or success) so nothing has duplicate or missing ownership, define an acceptance criterion and a verification method per item, and set a daily reporting cadence with a report template. Acceptance criteria: a roadmap table with columns item, owner profile, priority, dependencies, acceptance criterion, verification method; every item has exactly one owner; the daily report template is included.

title: Define control-plane contracts: task schema, events, MCP manifest, routing
body:
GOAL: Publish the canonical contracts that let Pilot, Kanban, Buzz, MCP, specialist bots, and the 31-agent orchestrator interoperate. Base every decision on the audit report from the parent task; where the audit found gaps, specify the target state explicitly.

DELIVERABLES:
(a) Canonical task object schema: id, title, body, assignee, parents[], status, artifacts[], timestamps, idempotency_key.
(b) Event bus topics and payload shapes: task.created, task.claimed, task.completed, task.failed, escalation.raised.
(c) MCP tool manifest conventions: naming scheme, input/output JSON schemas, auth scope per tool, required safety parameters (dry_run flag, idempotency key).
(d) Routing rules mapping task categories to profiles (board, engineering, guardian, hunter, operations, pilot, platform, sales, success) plus the default fallback.
(e) Per-channel rate limits and global/per-agent kill-switch flag definitions.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: Versioned contract document committed to the repo with machine-readable schemas; schemas validate against at least one real payload from the audit; operations confirms the routing rules leave no task category without an owner.

title: Wire Pilot to Kanban via cua-driver for card pull and status updates
body:
GOAL: Bidirectional Pilot↔Kanban bridge so desktop work flows through the board instead of ad-hoc commands. Implement strictly against the contract published by the parent task.

BEHAVIOR:
1. Poll the Kanban board on an interval for cards assigned to 'pilot' in a runnable state.
2. For each card: claim it (move to in-progress, emit task.claimed), parse the body as the work spec, execute the described hands-on action on the Windows PC via cua-driver (clicks, typing, background screenshots).
3. On completion: move the card to done, attach the screenshot artifact, post a summary comment, emit task.completed.
4. On failure: move the card to a blocked state with a structured reason, emit task.failed, never silently retry more than the contract's limit.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: One demo card travels end-to-end (created → claimed → completed with screenshot artifact attached) with zero manual intervention, and the failure path is demonstrated once with a clean blocked-state transition. All messages conform to the contract schemas.

title: Expose Buzz voice/WhatsApp/email actions as safe MCP tools
body:
GOAL: Make the Buzz outbound channels (voice call, WhatsApp message, email) callable by any specialist bot through MCP, with safety rails built in. Implement against the contract from the parent task.

REQUIREMENTS PER TOOL:
- Registered in the MCP server tool manifest with full input/output JSON schema and scoped auth.
- Mandatory dry_run parameter that validates inputs and simulates the send without touching the real channel.
- Idempotency key handling so a retried call cannot produce a duplicate send.
- Enforcement of the contract's per-channel rate limits.
- Pre-send check against DND/suppression lists discovered in the audit; suppressed targets are rejected with a structured reason.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: All three tools appear in MCP discovery; dry-run invocations succeed for valid inputs and fail cleanly for invalid/suppressed ones; exactly one real sandbox-environment send succeeds per tool and appears exactly once in the channel logs.

title: Register specialist bots and configure 31-agent orchestrator routing
body:
GOAL: Turn the orchestrator from configuration into a running router. Using the contract and routing rules from the parent task:

1. Register every specialist bot with its profile name, capability description, escalation path, and health-check endpoint. Close the gap between the current roster and the target of 31 agents, or document explicitly why fewer are registered and what replaces the remainder.
2. Load the routing table so each task category maps to exactly one primary profile with the agreed default fallback; verify no category is unowned.
3. Enable per-agent and global kill switches as defined in the contract, wired to the event bus.
4. Confirm dependency handling: tasks with parents are dispatched only after all parents complete; parentless tasks fan out in parallel.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: Orchestrator lists all registered agents with healthy status; in staging, one synthetic task per major category routes to the correct profile; killing a single agent via its switch stops only that agent while the global switch halts dispatch entirely.

title: Run E2E control-plane verification and issue go/no-go verdict
body:
GOAL: Independent end-to-end verification that the control plane actually runs as a system, then a formal verdict on the parent CTRL-P task. You are independent of the builders — judge only observed behavior.

E2E SCENARIO: Create a test lead-gen task → orchestrator routes it to hunter → hunter output triggers a Buzz MCP tool in dry-run mode → pilot executes one benign desktop step → all status transitions propagate back to the Kanban card automatically.

SAFETY CHECKS:
- Zero duplicate sends across repeated tool invocations with identical idempotency keys.
- Rate limits reject excess calls with structured errors.
- Global kill switch halts all agent activity within seconds of activation.
- Failed-task escalation fires and lands on an owned queue.
- Tenant isolation/RBAC holds on every board and tool interaction observed.

VERDICT: Post PASS / PASS_WITH_RISK / FAIL / BLOCKED to the parent CTRL-P task with evidence links. On PASS or PASS_WITH_RISK, request board authorization for production go-live; on FAIL or BLOCKED, list each blocking defect with a named owning profile.

title: Audit pipeline: flag stale and blocked leads with reasons
body:
GOAL: Deliver a concrete stale/blocked-lead audit of the sales pipeline so the Owner can act on it during Revenue Sprint Cycle-1 (day 1 of 7, target Rs 5,00,000).

CONTEXT: Swarm root / shared blackboard is task t_3c887faa. If the snapshot is missing, wait/re-check before proceeding rather than guessing.

APPROACH:
1. From the snapshot data, identify: (a) STALE leads — no activity/touch beyond the sprint-relevant threshold (e.g., no follow-up in 14+ days), (b) BLOCKED leads — stuck in a stage due to missing info, failed sends, pending owner action, or system errors.
2. For each flagged lead: lead ID/reference, current stage, days since last touch, reason it is stale/blocked, and ONE recommended next action (e.g., 'draft follow-up email', 'owner review needed', 'fix send failure').

title: Verify dialer readiness: VPS scheduler, DND fail-closed, TRAI window
body:
GOAL: Certify whether the outbound dialer is SAFE and READY for Revenue Sprint Cycle-1 calling, or list exactly what blocks it.

CONTEXT: Swarm root / shared blackboard is task t_3c887faa. Hard guardrail being verified: outbound calling ONLY via the VPS scheduler, with DND handling FAIL-CLOSED (if DND status cannot be confirmed, the call must NOT go out) and the TRAI calling window left untouched/unmodified.

APPROACH:
1. Verify the VPS scheduler service is deployed, reachable, and healthy (check status/health endpoint or logs; coordinate facts via root t_3c887faa if another worker already pulled them).
2. Verify DND/suppression logic: confirm the scheduler consults the DND list BEFORE dialing and that a DND lookup failure results in NO call placed (fail-closed), not a skipped-check. Inspect code path/config or run a safe dry-run test if available.
3. Verify TRAI calling-window configuration exists and has NOT been altered (report the configured window values as-is; do not change them).
4. Check rate limits/idempotency: confirm no duplicate-call risk and that call volume caps are set.
5. Confirm payment-related flows are NOT wired into the dialer (payment/UPI confirmations are owner-only; any automation touching money steps is a BLOCKER).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Verdict posted as a structured comment on root t_3c887faa using guardian semantics: PASS / PASS_WITH_RISK / FAIL / BLOCKED, with evidence for each check (scheduler health, DND fail-closed proof, TRAI window values, rate-limit config).
- If FAIL/BLOCKED: list the specific minimal fixes required, ranked by how quickly they restore compliant calling.
- Completion metadata includes machine-readable facts: {scheduler_healthy: bool, dnd_fail_closed: bool, trai_window: str, verdict: str}.
- Do NOT place any real outbound calls and do NOT modify scheduler/DND/TRAI configuration — verification only.
